gi6_plans.topic: Annexation pledges 2019-20, the Trump plan, the UAE suspension, the 2022 coalition deal and Smotrich's civil powers

claims.text: On 10 Sep 2019, a week before the 17 Sep election, Netanyahu pledged to extend Israeli sovereignty over the Jordan Valley (nearly a quarter of the West Bank) shortly after forming a government, and later to annex settlements: 'a one-time opportunity, to extend Israeli sovereignty on our settlements in Judea and Samaria'; linked timing to Trump's forthcoming plan. Abbas said all agreements would be cancelled; Jordan's FM Safadi: 'a serious escalation that undermines all peace efforts'; UN spokesman: 'devastating' to two-state prospects; Lapid: 'an election stunt'; US officials briefed in advance raised no objection.

Trump plan released 28 Jan 2020: Israel would gain sovereignty over about 30% of the West Bank, including settlements and most of the Jordan Valley; Palestinians could get a demilitarized state in non-contiguous areas linked by roads/bridges/tunnels, capital in Abu Dis or near East Jerusalem, conditional on criteria including disarming Hamas and recognizing Israel as 'the nation state of the Jewish people'; four years to meet conditions; Pompeo said US would support annexation consistent with the maps; Netanyahu said his government would consider measures to effectively annex settlements and the Jordan Valley.

Netanyahu-Gantz coalition agreement signed 20 Apr 2020, clause 29: Netanyahu could bring the agreement reached with the US on applying sovereignty to cabinet and/or Knesset 'starting July 1, 2020', in full agreement with the US including on maps, while 'maintaining regional stability' and existing peace agreements. Erekat: 'Annexation means the end of any possibility for a negotiated solution.'

Joint US-Israel-UAE statement of 13 Aug 2020: 'Israel will suspend declaring sovereignty over areas outlined in the President's Vision for Peace' and focus on expanding ties with the Arab and Muslim world.

14 Aug 2020: Netanyahu said annexation 'remains on the table' and there was 'no change' in his plan, in coordination with the US; Trump: 'It's off the table' (could not speak about the future); Ambassador Friedman: 'suspend' was 'chosen carefully', a 'temporary halt', off the table now 'but it's not off the table permanently'.

Likud-Religious Zionism coalition agreement of 1 Dec 2022: the prime minister 'will work towards the formulation and promotion of a policy whereby sovereignty is applied' to Judea and Samaria; Smotrich to take a ministerial post in the Defense Ministry overseeing West Bank civil matters; on 23 Feb 2023 Defense Minister Gallant signed an agreement assigning governmental powers in the West Bank to a body headed by Smotrich.

Smotrich recorded 9 Jun 2024 at a West Bank settlers' gathering (recording supplied by a Peace Now researcher, reviewed by the NYT): 'We created a separate civilian system'; 'it's mega-dramatic'; 'Such changes change a system's DNA'; Defense Ministry kept involved so 'It will be easier to swallow in the international and legal context', 'So that they won't say that we are doing annexation here'; said Netanyahu was 'with us full on'. Smotrich's spokesman confirmed the speech; PM's office: final status 'will be determined by the parties in direct negotiations', 'This policy has not changed.'

gi6_votes.topic: 2024-25 sovereignty statements, the 82% plan, the UAE red line, US positions and the Knesset readings

claims.text: 11 Nov 2024, at his Knesset faction meeting, Smotrich posted '2025: the year of sovereignty in Judea and Samaria' and said 'I have directed the start of professional work to prepare the necessary infrastructure' (Settlement Directorate and Civil Administration); 'The only way to remove this danger from the agenda is to apply Israeli sovereignty.' FM Gideon Saar: 'A decision has not yet been made on the issue.' PA spokesman Abu Rudeineh said the remarks confirmed intent to annex.

3 Sep 2025 Smotrich unveiled a proposal to annex 82% of the West Bank with a map; guiding principle 'maximum territory and minimum Arab population'; six Palestinian population centres (Ramallah, Nablus, Jenin, Tulkarem, Jericho, Hebron) left as enclaves; called on Netanyahu 'to convene the government to approve applying sovereignty'; statement: 'Preventing a Palestinian state is an Israeli consensus'; 'Sovereignty takes the idea off of the global agenda'; on PA opposition: 'we will destroy them just as we do Hamas'; Huckabee reportedly told ministers the US was 'extremely concerned' about PA collapse.

3 Sep 2025: a senior Emirati official said annexation would be a 'red line' for the UAE, 'a death knell for the two-State solution', 'The choice before Israel right now is annexation or integration'; Lana Nusseibeh: 'We trust that President Trump will not allow the Abraham Accords tenet of his legacy to be tarnished'; Israeli officials said the 2020 commitment was time-bound and had expired; no decision made. ToI also reports Nusseibeh called annexation a 'red line'.

11 Sep 2025 at Ma'ale Adumim Netanyahu signed a framework agreement advancing E1: 'We are going to fulfill our promise that there will be no Palestinian state; this place belongs to us'; Smotrich said Israel would soon celebrate applying sovereignty.

25 Sep 2025 in the Oval Office Trump said: 'I will not allow Israel to annex the West Bank... It's not going to happen'; 'It's been enough. It's time to stop now.' Context: about 10 states including Britain, France, Australia recognized Palestine that week; UAE called annexation a 'red line'.

22 Oct 2025 preliminary readings: Avi Maoz (Noam) bill to 'apply its laws and sovereignty to the areas of settlement in Judea and Samaria' passed 25-24, Yuli Edelstein (Likud) casting the decisive vote and then removed from the Foreign Affairs and Defense Committee; Liberman (Yisrael Beytenu) bill on Ma'ale Adumim passed 32-9 with Lapid and Gantz in favour; Likud boycotted, calling the bills 'trolling... aimed at damaging our relations with the US' and saying 'true sovereignty will be achieved not with a show-off law for the protocol'; both need three more readings; referred to the FADC.

gi6_ground.topic: Land registration (Feb 2026), the E1 tender (Aug-Oct 2026) and status before the 27 Oct 2026 election

claims.text: 15 Feb 2026 cabinet decision: West Bank land registration in Area C, NIS 244.1m (~$78m) over four years, up to 35 staff, run by the Justice Ministry, target 15% of Area C in five years; unclaimed land automatically becomes state land; only about one-third of the West Bank was registered before 1967, after which Israel froze registration. Joint Katz-Levin-Smotrich statement: 'the registration of extensive areas in Judea and Samaria that belong to the state'; Levin: 'a real revolution in Judea and Samaria'. Peace Now: 'a mega land grab of Palestinian property'; Yesh Din's Shlomo Zacharia: process favours whoever holds the land.

Reuters 15 Feb 2026: first West Bank land registration since 1967; Smotrich: 'We are continuing the revolution of settlement and strengthening our hold across all parts of our land'; Katz: a 'vital security measure designed to ensure control, enforcement, and full freedom of action'; cabinet: an 'appropriate response to illegal land registration processes promoted by the Palestinian Authority'; PA presidency: 'a de-facto annexation of occupied Palestinian territory and a declaration of the commencement of annexation plans'; Trump has ruled out annexation but not moved to curb settlement.

E1 tender for 1,234 units (about one-third of 3,401 approved) published 18 Aug 2026 by the Housing Ministry, bids closing 19 Oct 2026, a week before the 27 Oct election; an earlier tender 460/2025 issued in January covered the full number; petition 4388-10-25 (Ir Amim, Bimkom, Peace Now, Bedouin-Palestinian residents) before Jerusalem District Court, which on 15 Jun 2026 rejected the state's dismissal motion and ordered a response by 1 Sep 2026. Peace Now: 'a last-minute maneuver'; building would 'ruin the possibility' of two states.

8 Sep 2026: Jerusalem District Court (Judge Nimrod Flax) refused to freeze the E1 tender, without ruling on legality of the plans; three petitions against plans for ~3,400 homes remain; court had refused to freeze plans in Oct and Nov 2025; state and municipality reject claims of a defective and discriminatory process.

26 Sep 2026: the Attorney General's Office ordered the E1 bid deadline pushed back one month, past the 27 Oct election, citing diplomatic sensitivity and 'reducing the concern that the tender could be used for prohibited election propaganda'; tender not cancelled; Ma'ale Adumim municipality said it would petition; mayor Guy Yifrach: 'We will not give up and will not allow E1 to be turned into a hostage.'
The Knesset dissolved on 17 Jul 2026; general election set for 27 Oct 2026; Channel 12 poll projected neither bloc reaching 61 (anti-Netanyahu parties 59, pro-Netanyahu bloc 51, Arab parties 10).

gi6_audit.topic: Audit re-checks for Part Six (21 Oct 2026)

claims.text: FMEP: decisions of the appointed official can be appealed, but once claims are resolved no further appeal is possible; heavy weight given to whoever currently controls the land (per Haaretz); criticized by the UN and Arab states, some with normalized ties.
Judge Flax: a temporary freeze prevents irreversible harm; no such danger 'because construction is still far away'; court likely to rule before physical change.

Volume wording for the 1 Dec 2022 clause (fuller rendering, with the timing qualifier): 'the prime minister will lead the formulation and advancement of policies within the framework of applying sovereignty in Judea and Samaria, while choosing the timing and weighing all of the State of Israel's national and international interests'; Wikipedia's shorter rendering (from ToI) omits the timing clause.
